### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, touching **13** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`  _(via runtimeTypes (symbol, a field of const object REFERENCE_INTEGRITY_RULES))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **4** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cc95f5e63e3c96acafa55378a57d06c086e7d639` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f6c30be837a91e3c6901233fa0b5b875b250f506` — the merge of head `700c21cbbd4a1bfd7af1c6ce1872ecb578fa4821` into base `cc95f5e63e3c96acafa55378a57d06c086e7d639`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f6c30be837a91e3c6901233fa0b5b875b250f506 && git checkout f6c30be837a91e3c6901233fa0b5b875b250f506
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin cc95f5e63e3c96acafa55378a57d06c086e7d639 700c21cbbd4a1bfd7af1c6ce1872ecb578fa4821 && git checkout -B drift-repro cc95f5e63e3c96acafa55378a57d06c086e7d639 && git merge --no-ff 700c21cbbd4a1bfd7af1c6ce1872ecb578fa4821

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cc95f5e63e3c96acafa55378a57d06c086e7d639
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs cc95f5e63e3c96acafa55378a57d06c086e7d639` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Seat answer · PR #24630 · patch round 1 open question 1 · `domain:spec` seat 2 · session `session_019oFY6Hi35J7atvgVFnmoaK` · 2026-10-19T21:19Z

Answering the dev's `needs_decision` in report `6277518348` on #24563, head `a0c24ab647`.

**Answer: A.** Re-pin `packages/objectql/src/protocol-duplicate-package-unprefixed-object.test.ts`, case "a name already claimed is refused up front, at the object, naming the rename", to two refusals:
1. first, the `ticket` object, with every existing assertion on it;
2. then `view/ticket_views` with `list-view-object-outside-closure` at `views[0].object`.

Every other assertion stays, the negative control and "everything else still copies" included.

**Why the seat answers this itself.** This is a fixture re-trued to behaviour already ruled, so it sits in a no-escalation class. The ruling is B (`6273946447`): a publish-mode write of a package's list view bound outside that package's closure is refused. The maintainer approved that refusal into 18.0. `duplicatePackage` writes its copies through the same door. In this case the `ticket` copy is refused, so the copy of `ticket_views` keeps the source's `ticket`. That is a view in the copy package bound to another package's object, with no declared dependency: exactly the binding the ruling refuses.

Before this PR, that view landed with an advisory and showed the source package's records in the copy. The second refusal is an accurate consequence, and the test should pin it rather than hide it. The test's own subject (the object refused up front, naming the rename) does not move.

**Not taken:**
- **B** (`duplicatePackage` reports the view as not attempted). It would add a second policy in the copy door for the same end state. It is also a `protocol.ts` change, while PR #24599 is in flight on that file.
- **C** (exempt the copies). It special-cases the rule, which the patch order forbids.

**Owed in the same commit:**
- The changeset's TO line and the PR body's door list name `duplicatePackage` beside `saveMetaItem` publish, draft promotion and `publishPackageDrafts`. The wording: a copied list view whose bound object stays outside the copy package's closure, for example because that object's own copy was refused, is refused with the same rule.
- The docs sentence in `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx` names it too, if that sentence lists the doors.

**Riders:**
- The three `packages/objectql` test files are added to the engine rider on #6367.
- The dogfood test `packages/qa/dogfood/test/view-container-cross-package-default.dogfood.test.ts` is declared on the `domain:cli` seat post #6024.

No open PR touches any of these four files (read in this act).

The PR stays draft until the re-pin is pushed, CI is green on that head, and a contract review of record (narrowing face) passes on it.

### ① Derived judgments

**The narrowing is the ruled one (ruling B, record 6273946447), and no wider. Right.**

- One predicate. At the head, `packageScopeInForce` (runtime-gate.ts, line 445) is the sole guard of both `narrowObjectsToPackageClosure` (line 419, byte-equivalent to the base's inline test) and the `packageScope` member the gate puts on the rule context (line 1121). The four closure limbs are untouched. A rule can be told "under a closure" exactly when `objects` was narrowed, and never otherwise.
- Only one reader. `AuthoringRuleContext.packageScope` is read by the reference-integrity suite's `validateListViewFieldRefs` member alone (reference-integrity-suite.ts, line 325), which hands it to the rule as `ListViewFieldRefOptions.packageScope`. A git grep of every non-test `.ts` under `packages/` finds no other reader of the member and no other direct caller of `validateListViewFieldRefs` or `narrowObjectsToPackageClosure`. The seven CLI callers of `runAuthoringRules` (compile, lint, validate, artifact-packages, author-time-rules, scaffold-validate) cannot reach it: `runAuthoringRules` (authoring-rules.ts, lines 2293-2305) builds the rule context from exactly `sduiManifest`, `loweredHookRefs` and `judgeFilter`, so even a run object that carried `packageScope` would drop it. The one runtime caller is `runtime-authoring-gate.ts` (line 1036), which passed `packageScope` before this PR.
- CLI and overlay keep skip 1. In `validateListViewFieldRefs` (head lines 823-827) an unresolvable binding returns silently unless `scope` is set; the empty-graph early return (line 686) is relaxed only under a scope. With no package, `resolveWritePackageScope` answers `undefined` (protocol.ts, line 7735 onward: no id, the `sys_metadata` sentinel, an unreadable package, no `getPackage`, a throw), the gate narrows nothing and states nothing. Pinned at both layers (lint "a write that names no package is unchanged", protocol (c)).
- Drafts are never gated: `evaluateRuntimeAuthoringGate` returns before any rule when `state !== 'active'` (runtime-authoring-gate.ts, D1), unchanged. Pinned by protocol (a) draft save.
- Nothing else now refuses. The rule's `runtimeTypes` stay `['flow', 'view', 'object']`; `validateObjectReferences` stays `['flow', 'dataset']` (line 224); the flow door's `flow-trigger-unknown-object` stays `warning` (validate-flow-trigger-readiness.ts, lines 448 and 500). On a `flow` write a stored sibling's out-of-closure built-in list view cancels in the differential (pinned). On an `object` write into a package, a built-in `listViews` entry that retargets `data.object` outside the closure is refused: that is a list view written into the package through the object door, inside the ruling, and the changeset says so.
- `OS_ALLOW_UNLINTED_METADATA_WRITES=1` (runtime-authoring-gate.ts, line 117) still downgrades the refusal to a logged write, unchanged.

**Every door the changeset's FROM / TO names is real. Right, with one precision note.**

- `saveMetaItem` publish: protocol.ts line 23738 calls `assertRuntimeAuthoringRules` with `packageId: request.packageId ?? null`; that gate resolves the closure (line 7432) and passes `packageScope` to `evaluateRuntimeAuthoringGate` (line 7472), which passes it to `runRuntimeAuthoringRules` (runtime-authoring-gate.ts, line 1039). REST `PUT /api/v1/meta/view/:name?package=` maps the query to `packageId` (meta-item-write-routes.ts, line 312). A verdict with an `error` finding throws `422 INVALID_METADATA` before the repository write. Pinned (a), (g).
- Draft promotion (`publishMetaItem`): `promoteDraftForPublish` (line 25447) runs the same gate with `state: 'active'` and `packageId` when the caller states one; the REST promote route forwards `?package=` (meta-item-history-routes.ts). Pinned (d). Precision: a promotion that states no package (a bare `POST .../publish` on a package-listed draft) resolves the row through `packagelessDraftAddress` but hands the gate no package, so it narrows nothing. protocol.ts documents this at lines 25455-25470 as the pre-existing unstated-package case, filed separately; it is unchanged here and falls under the changeset's "a write that names no package is judged against the whole collection". Not a FAIL item.
- `publishPackageDrafts`: each draft is promoted through `promoteDraftForPublish` with `packageId: d.packageId` (the row's own binding) and the batch's `pending` declarations (lines 26760-26805); a throw tags the causal item and rolls the batch back. Pinned (e), with (f) showing a same-batch drafted object is kept by limb 2 (no provenance) so there is no phantom refusal.
- `duplicatePackage`: every copy is written by `saveMetaItem({ mode: 'publish', packageId: request.targetPackageId })` (lines 28363-28372); the 422 is caught into `failed[]` with `clientFacingFailureText` (line 28399), whose message lists each issue as `path [rule]` (runtime-authoring-gate.ts, line 1145), which is the locator the re-pinned test asserts. The target manifest is `...srcPkg.manifest` (line 28195), so a declared dependency is inherited by the copy. Seat answer A's mechanism is accurate: with the `ticket` copy refused, the copied `ticket_views` keeps `object: 'ticket'` (owner P), P is not in Q's closure, and the save door refuses it at `views[0].object` (the view has no `data.object`; the fallback key is the container's `object`, head lines 969-970 and 997-1003).
- Doors that write a package's list view and are not listed: `rollbackMetaItem` (line 29888) and `revertCommit` (line 29326) restore a history body through `repo.restoreVersion` with `restoredBodyWriter` (line 7181), which judges only the name and the permission-set owner binding and runs no authoring rule. They are not publish-mode writes of an authored body, they pre-date this PR for every rule, and the changeset's "the door judges writes only" does not claim them. Named for the seat; not a FAIL item.

**The finding. Right.**

- `severity: 'error'` (validate-list-view-field-refs.ts, line 703), rule `list-view-object-outside-closure`, one per list view: `reportOutsideClosure` runs once in `checkListView` and returns before the positions (lines 823-826), so field positions stay unjudged for that view. Skip 2 (`!graph.get(object)`, line 827) is unchanged. Skip 4 (a non-`object` provider) still precedes it.
- Path: `bindingPathOf` (line 929) names `PATH.data.object` when the list view declares `data.object`, else the container's `objectName` / `object` (`viewObjectPath`), else `objects[N].name` for a built-in list view. Pinned at `views[0].data.object` (protocol) and `views[0].object` (the duplicate case).
- Message and hint are true. One wording note: the message's parenthetical describes the closure as "its own objects, the objects of the packages its manifest declares in dependencies, and platform objects", three of the four limbs; it omits provenance-less overlay rows. An author who sees the message bound an object outside all four limbs, so the omission cannot mislead; the hint's two arms (declare the dependency, or bind inside the closure) are the remedy for both the undeclared and the nonexistent case.
- `suggestName(object, graph.keys())` (object-graph.ts, line 610) draws from the graph built from `stack.objects`, which under a closure is the narrowed collection, so no name outside the closure is leaked. The CLI never reaches this branch.

**The four fixture re-trues outside the claim. Right.**

- `publish-package-drafts-response-conformance.test.ts`: `viewBody` binds `sys_metadata` instead of `case`. The harness registers `sys_metadata` with an `id` field (lines 41-60), and the `sys_` prefix keeps it in every closure. No assertion changed. The check is stronger, not weaker: before, `case` existed nowhere and the view was skipped silently; now the view is judged and stays advisory-free on its own merits, and the `byte-stability` case no longer passes on an empty `published[]`.
- `protocol-duplicate-package-names-in-step.test.ts`: the source manifest declares `dependencies: { [R]: '*' }`. The test's subject (an object outside the package keeps its name in the copy) is unchanged; the copy inherits the declaration through `...srcPkg.manifest`. No assertion changed.

That is the ruled consequence, as seat answer A states.
- `view-container-cross-package-default.dogfood.test.ts`: the `POST /packages` manifest declares `dependencies: { [SHOWCASE]: '*' }`, which `ManifestSchema` accepts (`z.record(z.string(), z.string())`, manifest.zod.ts line 715). The dev's control (without the declaration, 422 and refused) is the refusal measured end to end through REST.

- Lint block, 11 new cases (file 27): three refusal cases assert `errors` / `advisories` by severity, the flow case asserts the object-door refusal in `errors`, the CLI case asserts rule ids only. Severity back to `warning` reds exactly those four and greens the other 23, as reported. The round-0 ablation (report removed) reds five, adding the scoped half of the CLI case, as reported.

- Controls pinned: declared dependency, system object by prefix and by `isSystem`, provenance-less overlay row, the empty package id, the overlay door (stranger column refused, nonexistent object silent), the flow verdict, the CLI reading, and a stored row that loads (`loaded: 1, errors: 0`) and is refused only at its next save.

**Changeset, semver, Clause-②. Right.**

- `'@objectstack/lint': minor`, title `fix(lint)!:`, `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` on the changeset (line 7) and the PR body (line 3). `yes (narrowing)` is the reader's spelling for widen plus narrow (clause2-line.mjs): the public surface grows by the optional `AuthoringRuleContext.packageScope`, the optional second argument of `validateListViewFieldRefs`, and the exports `LIST_VIEW_OBJECT_OUTSIDE_CLOSURE` and `ListViewFieldRefOptions`, and the save door's accept set narrows. Nothing is removed or renamed. The claim's `no (narrowing)` was amended to this in 6273958360, and the rider addendum 6277575090 carries the amended line.

- `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` is right. The body carries no framed rewrite (no migration heading, no arrow or table rewrite under one), which is what `findMigrationPrescription` refuses; `unpublished` is closed because `@objectstack/lint` publishes; `already-registered` and `registered` have no ledger id to name; `runtime-interface-only`, `type-surface-only` and `runtime-export-retired` do not describe a door verdict. The marker's own closing of each category is accurate. `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, the job that runs the gate, is green on this head.
- The `.changeset/pre.json` parenthetical is true on `main`: the file reads `{"mode": "exit", "tag": "next"}`, and `@objectstack/lint` sits at `18.0.0-next.5`, so the next version pass cuts 18.0.0.
- Siblings: `24491-page-save-door-visibility-predicates.md` and `24468-lint-rule-hop-undeclared-field.md` carry the same shape (`minor`, `!`, FROM / TO / Fix, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`) with `no (narrowing)` because neither grew the public surface; this one differs only in the arm, and rightly.

**Docs. Right.** The `validating-metadata.mdx` sentence ("never which rules run" and "one rule is told the closure is in force ... refused with `list-view-object-outside-closure` instead of having its field references skipped") is true: `runtimeAuthoringRulesFor(type)` is unchanged, nothing at the door walks `packages[]`, and the one rule is the one above.
